_provenance.what: Three real merged promotion PRs from datanika-core, captured verbatim: the PR body as GitHub stores it, and GitHub's own closingIssuesReferences answer for that PR. These are NOT hand-written fixtures. A hand-written body would encode our model of the defect, which is the one thing it cannot be used to check (QA_RULES section 6).
_provenance.how: gh api graphql -f query='{ repository(owner:"datanika-io", name:"datanika-core") { pullRequest(number:N) { body closingIssuesReferences(first:50){nodes{number state}} } } }'

roles.1526: the narrative instance. A sentence written to say the issue would NOT close. Must be flagged: 1477 is in GitHub's closing set and the generated block declares only 1507.
roles.1188: the in-block instance, and the reason the originally-specified design was withdrawn. promotion_refs.py rendered a promoted issue's TITLE into the generated block, and that title carried a closing keyword and a number. A guard that skips the block -- which is what the acceptance criteria originally said to build -- is structurally blind to it.
roles.1519: the false-positive control. Both references intended and both declared. A guard that flags everything is one careless repair away from permitting everything, so this one passing is not optional.

_provenance.population: Re-derived over 309 merged PRs into a default branch across both repos: 125 carry a generated block, and 6 of those 125 disagree with the oracle. The other 119 agree exactly. Re-derive rather than quoting these counts; the corpus grows.

1526.title: [Infra] Promote dev → master (2026-09-23 round-14 batch)
1526.body:
Bundled release: the accessibility batch that has been blocking [core#720]'s graduation for five
rounds, the run-cancellation audit trail, QA's supersession grading, and the Grafana watchdog.

**11 commits.** The `Closes`/`refs` block below is generated by `Promotion PR refs` from the commits
actually being promoted — I have not hand-enumerated it.

## What ships

**Accessibility — [core#1409], five of six violation classes plus the grey-text half of the sixth.**
The accent decision (`violet` / `mauve`, `solid` reserved for scales that clear 4.5:1 at step 9) is
merged as `SPEC_BUTTON_CONTRAST.md` and four commits build against it: `/settings` inputs are named,
links in sentences are underlined, grey text moves to Radix step 11 rather than the steps designed
for fills, and the legibility guard learned to see a colour written as a `cond`.

⚠️ **This does NOT graduate [core#720].** The **button theme** is still unbuilt — it is Engineering's
this round — and QA re-derived 3 of 6 classes on `dev` / **zero on `master`** yesterday. What this
promotion changes is that number: the classes on `dev` reach `master`, so QA can re-measure against
production instead of against a branch. **It is not "one PR away" and never was.**

**Run cancellation — [core#657].** A UI cancel now writes an audit row naming who stopped the run,
shipped red-first (the failing test is its own commit). The cancel dialog's last clause named
*uploads* while the dialog renders for every `Run.target_type`; that is corrected here and in the
landing copy promoted alongside.
⚠️ **The worker-side stop is NOT in this batch** and still blocks [core#1354] AC3.

**Supersession — [core#1507], closes.** A run skipped by supersession ran nothing; it is now graded,
counted and said so, instead of being scored as if it had passed.

**Grafana watchdog — [core#1477], `refs` not `closes`, deliberately.** An external watchdog plus the
first cron entry that lives in git, installed by `install-server-scripts.sh` under a new
`INSTALL_CRON` category. **I will close #1477 by hand only after `/etc/cron.d/datanika` is on the box
and the job has actually run** — which is the standard the change itself exists to enforce, so
closing it on merge would be the defect it was written against.

## Gate — read on the exact head `e1aead75`, not on a PR rollup

| gate | reading |
|---|---|
| all workflow runs on `e1aead75` | `CI` success, `Build & push image` success — **0 rows** not `completed/success` |
| the six required checks | `lint`, `test`, `helm-lint`, `migration-roundtrip`, `image-probe`, `cloud-suite` — all success |
| `staging / {deploy,smoke,e2e}-staging` | all success; **0 cancelled jobs** in the run |
| `verify_e2e_attribution.py --sha e1aead75` | **exit 0** — all three attributed to this commit's own build, every job an actual reading |
| `image-cve` | success |
| cloud `compare/master...dev` | **`identical`** — the pairing gate will pass |
| migrations in batch | **0 files** (57 files changed total, so the diff can see) |
| in-flight `dev` runs / queue / open PRs | 0 / 0 / 0 |

**Zero migrations, so the expand/contract `t1` window carries no risk this time** — the
previously-deployed code cannot meet a new schema because there is no new schema.

**Celery restart:** in-flight runs checked on the box before merging. Live `schedules` is **0** —
read with `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`, which is the only query that answers it; a bare `count(*)`
returns 1 because of a soft-deleted row whose `is_active` is still `true`.

Serving colour before this deploy is **green** (`datanika-app-b`, 8010/3010), so this one lands on
blue. Disk 35% used, 99 GiB free.

1188.title: [Infra] Promote dev to master — the tree reconciler, QA guard fixes, locale spec
1188.body:
## Promotion: `dev` → `master` (9 commits, 4 departments)

Cloud is `identical` to its own `master`, so the [core#1123] deploy gate is satisfied and there is
no cloud promotion to sequence ahead of this one.

### What ships

| commit | |
|---|---|
| `4354ccf` | [Product] Spec locale reachability and consistency — refs #696, #695 |
| `13e9fdb` | [Engineering] Cover the half of #1010's guard that no test could see — refs #1010 |
| `adf7caa` `908b432` `33f0088` | [QA] `--stdin` refuses a concatenated stream; the guard crashed on the one path that has a finding; refuse a commit that closes an issue its subject only refs — **closes #1162** |
| `68d1887` | [Engineering] A row count we failed to read is not zero, and pin the dlt default SUCCESS rests on — refs #1170 |
| `cd4107e` `2f76ab9` `45e3bfe` | [Infra] The tree reconciler — refs #1178, refs #746 |

⚠️ **`closes #1162` is live in this batch** and will fire when this reaches the default branch. That
is QA's intent, flagged here only so it is not a surprise.

### The Infra change is the one that mutates production behaviour

`tar xzf` overwrites what the archive holds and removes nothing it omits, so **a file deleted in git
was never deleted from the box**. Measured after `master fe0a9823`: 822 shared, 0 missing, 11
box-only — five genuinely retired, six box-owned including `.env.docker`, its two operator backups
and **a Google OAuth client secret** under `.secrets/`.

🚨 The reconciler therefore keys on the **previous manifest, never on git**: a "delete anything
absent from the repo" rule deletes that credential on its first run. Box-owned state is
structurally unreachable, not merely deny-listed.

**This deploy is the reconciler's first run, and it will be a SEED run** — no manifest exists on the
box yet, so the manifest diff removes nothing and only the bootstrap graveyard fires.

**Prediction to check on the box afterwards**, computed against the measured listing:

```
REMOVED retired scripts/backup-postgres.sh
REMOVED retired scripts/setup-backup-cron.sh
REMOVED retired scripts/verify-backup.sh
REMOVED retired tests/test_deploy/test_workflow_secret_masking_executes.py
REMOVED retired tests/test_migrations/test_autocommit_block_availability.py
reconcile: no previous manifest — seeding … removing nothing on a seed run, by design.
```

Anything else removed, or any box-owned path named, is a defect — check before celebrating.

### Verification before promoting

`scripts/verify_e2e_attribution.py --sha 45e3bfe` — every staging verdict attributed to **this**
commit, with `e2e-staging` returning an actual `PASS` rather than merely going un-overtaken.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01373MPoUkPZsAgHgGTBRiiS

The list is derived mechanically and the closure stays a judgement — review each and close the ones whose acceptance criteria are fully met._

- #696 — [QA] The locale switcher is behind the auth wall, so every translated string on /login, /signup and password reset is unreachable · via #1179, commit 4354ccf
- #746 — scripts/verify-backup.sh runs a full restore inside the PRODUCTION postgres instance, and its assertion is vacuous · via commit cd4107e

1519.title: [Infra] Promote dev → master (2026-09-23 batch): run cancellation, Grafana WAL, monitoring pins, load-test harness
1519.body:
Second core promotion of the cycle — the one held on 2026-09-22 until it could carry the Grafana WAL conversion. 16 commits.

## Why this was held, and why it ships now

The hold was deliberate, not a queue. After #1505's deploy recreated Grafana, `max-retries-reached` hit **4** with retry depth reaching its ceiling of 3, and the box's IO full-stall share measured **9–20% all day** — so "promote during a quiet window" was not available as a remedy, because there is no quiet window. Adding another build to a margin measured at zero, without the fix, would have repeated it.

[core#1476]'s fix is now on `dev` (#1514), so the promotion carries its own remedy: the deploy stops Grafana, converts its SQLite to write-ahead logging while the file is closed, and only then recreates it.

**Baseline read on production immediately before this promotion (2026-09-23 12:22Z):** `grafana.db` header bytes 18/19 are `01 01` — still rollback-journal, so the conversion is genuinely pending and this deploy is its first run. `database is locked` appears **360 times** in the last 24h of Grafana's log, `max-retries-reached` **4**. Those are the numbers the next promotion should be measured against.

## What is in the batch

- **Run cancellation reaches production** — the `CANCELLING` status and its status sets (#657), the Cancel control on `/runs` (#657, #1354), and the prose that says what cancelling does. This is what unblocks core#1232's downstream and clears cloud #252's one designed red.
- **Grafana SQLite → WAL** (#1476) — conversion during the deploy's monitoring reload, plus a step that reports the journal mode by reading the *running* database's `-wal`/`-shm` files rather than asking Grafana's settings API. That distinction is the whole finding: the settings API reported `database.wal = true` while the file was still `journal_mode=delete`.
- **Every monitoring image pinned to version AND digest** (#1478) — they all floated on `:latest` while the deploy runs `--force-recreate prometheus grafana blackbox` on every promotion, so any promotion could have moved a version underneath configuration validated against a specific one, with no diff to show it. Docker Hub's `grafana/grafana:latest` had already moved off the digest production runs.
- **The load-test harness lands in `scripts/loadtest/`** (#778) — five defects found by running it, plus the latency-abort fix and a rehearsal that proves the abort criteria discriminate (A/B/C = 99/0/99). The instrument ships before the number, per the standing rule.
- Accessibility control names (#1409), the REST API header field (#1467), a superseded-OAuth-flow notice (#624), E2E API-budget fixes and the local-run-is-not-evidence guard (#1232, #1296).

## Promotion gate — read on the exact head `ffbdaff5`, not on a rollup

- All **six** required checks `completed:success`: `lint`, `test`, `helm-lint`, `migration-roundtrip`, `image-probe`, `cloud-suite`. Re-derived from branch protection rather than from a doc; `strict=true`, `allow_force_pushes=false`.
- `staging / deploy-staging`, `staging / smoke-staging`, `staging / e2e-staging` all `success` **on this head** — a promotion CD run carries no staging verdict of its own, so this is the only place that reading exists.
- `scripts/verify_e2e_attribution.py --sha ffbdaff5` exits **0**: `smoke-staging`, `e2e-staging` and `e2e-sso` each `attributed`, verdict `PASS`, against their own deploy at 2026-09-22T19:39:13Z. No `misattributed`, no `no_reading`, no `absent`.
- `image-cve` is `success` on this head — no fixable OS-package finding pending.
- No cancelled runs on the head. `datanika-cloud` `compare/master...dev` reads **identical**, so the cloud pairing gate passes and cloud is not behind.

## Risk review

- **No migrations in this batch.** The expand/contract `t1` window does not apply — `CANCELLING` is added to a `StrEnum` stored via `native_enum=False`, so there is no DDL and no constraint to widen.
- **Zero in-flight runs on production** (`running`/`pending`/`queued` = 0), so the Celery recreate interrupts nothing.
- **The one real blue/green window**: during the swap the retiring colour runs the pre-`CANCELLING` code. It cannot encounter the new value — the Cancel control ships in this same batch, so nothing could have written `cancelling` before it, and `announce_completion` refuses a non-terminal status regardless.
- Disk 99 GiB free (35% used), well clear of the deploy's 20 GiB warning band and 5 GiB floor.
- Serving **blue** (`datanika-app`, 8000/3000) at promotion time, so this deploy swaps to green.

## What to watch after the deploy

The WAL conversion is **fail-safe by design** — a failed conversion is a `::warning::` and Grafana starts in its previous journal mode, never a deploy that fails or a Grafana that does not come back. So its success is *not* asserted by a green deploy. Read it two ways: the `Report Grafana's SQLite journal mode` step, and the header bytes on the file itself.
